newsitem.title: UK: C&W pledges strong, stable China relationship.
newsitem.headline: C&W pledges strong, stable China relationship.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc, Britain's second biggest telecommunications company, said on Friday there was uncertainty on the eve of Hong Kong's reversion to Chinese rule but promised its relationship with China was soundly based.

"China is a country that values long relationships, and so do we," chairman Brian Smith told shareholders at the annual meeting. "Both sides have a stake in each others' prosperity and there is every reason to expect a strong, stable relationship in the future."

C&W earlier this month signed a landmark deal with China, selling an initial 5.5 percent stake for 726 million stg in its most lucrative asset -- Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd -- that provides about 65 percent of its profits.
In return for growth opportunities on the booming Chinese mainland, C&W will sell its Hong Kong Telecom stake down to 30 percent, with China Telecom taking the other 30 percent.

Hong Kong reverts to Chinese control at midnight on June 30. And some analysts have voiced concern that although the potential for growth in China is indisputable, the ability to make attractive returns for investments in that growth remains unproven.

Smith said that building on C&W's experience with Australian carrier Optus and Hong Kong Telecom, the group's new telephone and cable television venture Cable and Wireless Communications would be the only UK operator offering full bandwidth access to the home.
CWC will offer information, entertainment and telephony down one line.

C&W has declined to comment on newspaper reports in Britain and Australia that it plans to buy another 24.5 percent stake in Optus Communications Pty Ltd, tipped by one newspaper to be worth 500 million pounds.

Speculation has centred on C&W buying out America's BellSouth Corp's Optus stake. The company has also been reported to have approached the Australian government about relaxing rules that limit foreign shareholders to 49 percent of Optus.
But the Australian government on Friday denied that C&W had approched it about raising its Optus stake.
